name: clawmetry-setup-openclaw
description: Pinned OpenClaw CLI for the setup-openclaw composite action. CI-only: nothing here ships in the clawmetry wheel or is imported by the dashboard.
//overrides: The openclaw pin is 2026.9.2 and the tree is advisory-clean. `npm audit`
reports 0 vulnerabilities. There is nothing held back here any more, so if
you are reading this looking for the blocker, there isn't one.
WHAT THIS CORRECTS. Until 2026-10-02 this note recorded the pin as frozen at
2026.5.12 behind a Node blocker: openclaw 2026.9.7 declares
`engines.node >=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`, the action's node-version default
is the bare major "22", so moving the pin was written up as a Node MAJOR
move for the whole E2E fleet across two repositories -- and the note told
the next reader to expect a bump PR to fail until that happened.
That was measured against 2026.9.7 ALONE, and it does not generalise. The
Node 24 floor is specific to 2026.9.7, the newest release. Measured
2026-10-02 with `npm view openclaw@<v> engines.node`:
2026.9.2 therefore installs on Node 22. `node-version` is the bare major, so
setup-node resolves the newest 22.x -- 22.23.3 today, comfortably above the
22.22.3 floor. No workflow changes major, and nothing in the fleet moves.
The second half of that note was wrong too. It read 'nine are on "20", three
on "22"' and concluded every setup-openclaw caller faced a Node move. Those
nine Node-20 workflows do not call this action. All six that do -- ci.yml
(live-openclaw-e2e), e2e-nightly.yml, moat-keystone-drive-nightly.yml,
openclaw-boot.yml, oss-golden-path.yml and pr-screenshots.yml -- take the
default, so all six get 22.x and none passes a node-version of its own.
WHAT THE BUMP CLEARS. Measured by regenerating the lockfile with only the
version changed, keeping the overrides below, and running `npm audit`:
before  3 packages / 25 advisories / 3 high
after   0 packages /  0 advisories
The three packages the old note called permanently uncoverable -- openclaw
itself (19 advisories), @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (4) and extract-zip
(2) -- are cleared because 2026.9.2 fixes its own and no longer depends on
the other two: pi-coding-agent, extract-zip, pdfjs-dist and basic-ftp all
leave the tree entirely. Those 25 were the WHOLE of what OSSF Scorecard
reports as this repository's VulnerabilitiesID, so that probe should go to
zero with this change.
This also retires the pi-coding-agent override question. It was never an
override problem: openclaw 2026.5.12 imported `AuthStorage` from that
package and 0.87.1 stopped exporting it, so the two had to move together.
Moving openclaw is what moves them together, and the package is now gone
from the tree, so there is nothing left to override.
WHY THE OVERRIDES STAY. They are still doing work -- not all of them, but
enough that removing the block is a regression. Measured at 2026.9.2 with
the overrides deleted and nothing else changed: undici comes back high and
openclaw moderate (2 advisories). So the block is kept, and each key's
resolution at 2026.9.2 was checked rather than assumed:
tar@7              7.5.22    load-bearing, at the hoisted root
undici@8           8.10.2    load-bearing  (this is the one that regresses)
ws@8               8.21.3    load-bearing
brace-expansion@5  5.0.12    load-bearing
fast-uri@3         3.1.8     load-bearing
ip-address@10      10.7.2    load-bearing
markdown-it@14     14.3.2    INERT -- package absent from the tree
basic-ftp          6.2.1     INERT -- package absent from the tree
pdfjs-dist@5       6.2.108   INERT -- package absent from the tree
The three inert keys are left in place deliberately: each is a no-op while
its package is absent, and each becomes correct again the moment a future
openclaw pulls that package back in. Delete them only with a fresh audit.
Keys stay range-scoped (name@major) for the original reason: a bare `undici`
key would also rewrite any undici@7 a transitive resolves, which is a major
bump for that consumer. `basic-ftp` is the one bare key, and the reason it
is safe is recorded with its 2026-10-01 measurement in git history -- the
tree held exactly one copy, both requesters on 5.x. It is inert now anyway.
RUN THE BOOT GATE FOR ANY CHANGE TO THIS FILE OR THE LOCKFILE. This is the
lesson that cost the most and it has not changed. `npm ci` succeeds and
`openclaw --version` prints a version even when the module graph is broken:
neither loads the graph. The gate that catches it is booting the gateway,
which is what .github/workflows/openclaw-boot.yml does:
openclaw gateway --port 18789 --verbose --allow-unconfigured
# then poll http://127.0.0.1:18789/ for any HTTP response
It reproduces locally in about five seconds and logs 'http server listening'
then 'ready' when the tree is sound. Run it, not just --version.
Boot gate run for THIS change, on Node 22.23.3: HTTP 200 after ~6s, 'http
server listening (13 plugins: anthropic, browser, canvas, cua-computer,
device-pair, file-transfer, geolocation, linux-node, memory-core, ollama,
openai, talk-voice, xai)', 'ready', 'heartbeat started', on OpenClaw 2026.9.2
(3928bad). No module-resolution error of the AuthStorage shape.
THE DAEMON SIDE IS READY, which is the other thing that used to hold this
pin. 2026.9.2 is past the 2026.5.28..2026.6.34 boundary where OpenClaw moved
per-session transcripts out of agents/main/sessions/*.jsonl and into
agents/<id>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite. #6233 shipped
clawmetry/openclaw_sqlite.py, which reads that store read-only and mirrors
it into the JSONL layout the daemon already ingests; its CHANGELOG entry
records a verified daemon ingest of a live OpenClaw 2026.9.7 store. Released
WHAT IS LEFT, as a future decision and not a blocker: 2026.9.7 is the only
release that needs Node 24. Taking it means raising this action's default
and moving every caller, for the difference between 2026.9.2 and 2026.9.7.
Nothing forces that today -- the tree is already advisory-clean at 2026.9.2.
The mirror of this action in vivekchand/clawmetry-cloud pins 2026.9.2 as
well, which is where that version came from: cloud has been running it in
CI, so this repository is adopting a version already proven there rather
than a fresh one. The two copies still share a mechanism rather than a
release cadence -- keep them in step on the mechanism, and let each pin what
its own suites are green against.
